A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Active Measurement: Efficient Estimation at Scale by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original bird-counting experiments on photographs and radar data, with estimation errors, confidence-interval evaluations, and supplementary analyses in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds malaria-cell and damaged-building counting evaluations in Sections 6–7 and Figure 7.

M1.justification: The sampling procedure, estimators, combined and inverse-variance weights, confidence-interval construction, and streaming algorithm remain unchanged. The new datasets use the existing method without introducing a new component.

E1.justification: v2 expands beyond bird photographs and weather radar to microscopy counting of malaria-infected cells using BBBC041v1 and satellite counting of damaged buildings using the Palu Tsunami subset of xBD. These add distinct biomedical and disaster-assessment domains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in corresponding experiments. Figure 7 uses existing MC and DIS variants; active testing and the PPI-motivated estimator in v2 Figure 6 were already evaluated in v1 Figure A8. The FamNet comparison also remains.

E3.justification: The added experiments specify initialization on three randomly selected cell images or five satellite images and use end-to-end adaptation with the existing image-detector settings. The retained bird and radar experiments keep their stated protocols and metrics.

E4.justification: Figure 7 extends the component comparisons separating adaptation and sampling without replacement to the two new domains, examining their benefits at different labeling fractions. Existing weighting sensitivity, proposal-quality, and fixed-checkpoint versus end-to-end analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 Figure A8 explicitly reports averaging over 10,000 simulations; this disclosure is omitted when its plots move into v2 Figure 6. Existing confidence-interval procedures and stated replication budgets otherwise remain, while the new Figure 7 reports 1,000 end-to-end trials.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds fractional-error results for malaria cells and damaged buildings. Radar coverage and interval-radius curves in Figures 5 and A7 also change, as do Figure 3 error-bar values. The original main error curves and table remain, including active-measurement errors of 0.23 at 40 labels and 0.06 at 200.

T1.justification: The propositions, assumptions, weighting bound, martingale limit arguments, and proofs in Appendices A–B are retained. Mathematical differences are limited to formatting and citation renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: interactive scientific measurement, unbiased and consistent estimators, novel weighting and uncertainty estimation, and reduced estimation error. The additional experiments support the existing broad applicability claim.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new results as evidence of domain generality and attributes differences from published DISCount building results to detector pretraining. Section 8 additionally discusses spatial autocorrelation in Reeds residuals and proposes Gaussian-process modeling; existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and documents initialization, target labels, and reuse of detector settings for the new tasks. The existing implementation, hardware, runtime, and data-processing details in Appendix C remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Five references are added concerning ecological counting, xBD, and microscopy datasets. Section 3 expands explanations of active testing and adaptive importance sampling and clarifies their relationship to active measurement, without substantially redefining the novelty position.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted related-work rewrites, adds task and result paragraphs, expands future work, and updates acknowledgments and the conference footer. The overall section structure is retained, with redundant Appendix D.6 material consolidated into the main text.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 7 and moves both panels of v1 Figure A8 into main-text Figure 6. Figure 3 gains dataset-size annotations and revised bar colors/hatching; confidence-interval plots receive color changes, and Figure 5 gains a clarifying caption.

improvement.justification: The new end-to-end evaluations provide useful evidence beyond bird counting, while the code pointer and clearer comparisons improve usability. v1 already included end-to-end validation in Appendix D.3, so this strengthens an existing evaluation. Reporting has small shortcomings: the moved baseline plots lose their explicit replication count, and the new malaria experiment does not explain the difference between 1,364 images in Section 6 and N=1,208 in Figure 7.
